# Certificate

`c.Certificate` calls the API's Certificate group. The certificate authorities
that the host trusts.

### List

```go
func (s *CertificateService) List(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
) (*Response[Collection[CertificateEntry]], error)
```

List the certificate authorities that the host trusts.

Lists each CA of the trust store through gohai: the distribution's and the local
ones on Linux, from the family's directories, and the system keychains on macOS,
each with its subject, fingerprint and expiry. A CA that osapi deployed reads by
the name that it was deployed with, not its file's osapi- name, and is managed.

It sends `GET /api/node/{hostname}/certificate`, and needs the permission
`certificate:read`.

The examples of the method's definition:

A Debian host with a system CA, `go run certificate.go list`:

```go
resp, err := c.Certificate.List(ctx, target)
```

### Create

```go
func (s *CertificateService) Create(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	input CertificateCreateInput,
) (*Response[Collection[CertificateResult]], error)
```

Add a certificate authority to the trust store.

Writes the PEM of the object as a file with the osapi- prefix, such as
osapi-internal-ca.crt for internal-ca, in the family's local directory:
/usr/local/share/ca-certificates on the Debian family, /etc/pki/trust/anchors on
SUSE, /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors on RHEL and Fedora. Then it rebuilds the
trust store: with update-ca-certificates on the Debian family and SUSE, and with
update-ca-trust on the others. Alpine reports skipped. A CA that osapi deployed
already with the same content does not change and reports changed: false. A file
of that name that osapi did not write is refused. macOS reports skipped.

It sends `POST /api/node/{hostname}/certificate`, and needs the permission
`certificate:write`.

The examples of the method's definition:

Add a CA, `go run certificate.go create`:

```go
resp, err := c.Certificate.Create(ctx, target, client.CertificateCreateInput{
	Name:   "internal-ca",
	Object: "internal-ca.pem",
})
```

### Get

```go
func (s *CertificateService) Get(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	name string,
) (*Response[Collection[CertificateEntry]], error)
```

Get one certificate authority.

Reads one CA from the same list, by the name that list gives it. A CA that the
host does not trust is not found. A name with a slash, such as a system CA of
the Debian family, is in list only.

It sends `GET /api/node/{hostname}/certificate/{name}`, and needs the permission
`certificate:read`.

The examples of the method's definition:

A CA that osapi deployed, by the name it was deployed with,
`go run certificate.go get`:

```go
resp, err := c.Certificate.Get(ctx, target, "internal-ca")
```

A CA of a Mac, `go run certificate.go get-2`:

```go
resp, err := c.Certificate.Get(ctx, target, "osapi example CA")
```

### Update

```go
func (s *CertificateService) Update(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	input CertificateUpdateInput,
) (*Response[Collection[CertificateResult]], error)
```

Write a certificate authority that osapi deployed again.

Writes the CA from the object, or from the one that it was deployed from when
the object is empty, and rebuilds the trust store when the file changed. A CA
that osapi did not deploy is not found. macOS reports skipped.

It sends `PUT /api/node/{hostname}/certificate/{name}`, and needs the permission
`certificate:write`.

The examples of the method's definition:

Write a CA from a new object, `go run certificate.go update`:

```go
resp, err := c.Certificate.Update(ctx, target, client.CertificateUpdateInput{
	Name:   "internal-ca",
	Object: "internal-ca-2.pem",
})
```

The object that it was deployed from, `go run certificate.go update-2`:

```go
resp, err := c.Certificate.Update(ctx, target, client.CertificateUpdateInput{Name: "internal-ca"})
```

### Delete

```go
func (s *CertificateService) Delete(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	name string,
) (*Response[Collection[CertificateResult]], error)
```

Remove a certificate authority that osapi deployed.

Removes the file of the CA and rebuilds the trust store: with
update-ca-certificates --fresh on the Debian family and SUSE, which removes the
links of the CA from /etc/ssl/certs, and update-ca-trust on the RHEL family. A
CA that osapi did not deploy does not change and reports changed: false: a
system CA is not osapi's to remove. macOS reports skipped.

It sends `DELETE /api/node/{hostname}/certificate/{name}`, and needs the
permission `certificate:write`.

The examples of the method's definition:

Remove a CA, `go run certificate.go delete`:

```go
resp, err := c.Certificate.Delete(ctx, target, "internal-ca")
```
